result:
PR #124 is pushed, ready, and relabelled `fold-ready`. The brief's resume steps are all done.

**Why attempt 3 did not finish.** It did finish its brief: selftest green, merged, pushed, marked ready, `harness` label on. The fold job then handed it back `needs-rebase` because PR #136 split `selftest.sh` into fragments after attempt 3's merge, and the 128-line block appended to `selftest.sh` conflicted with a file that no longer holds any checks. That is now recorded at the top of `docs/lanes/boardgate/NOTES.md`.

**What this attempt did.**
- Merged `origin/master` twice. The first merge conflicted only in `selftest.sh`. I took master's version verbatim and carried the block byte-identical into `docs/testing/jobs/selftest.d/97-board-gate.sh` behind a header in the other fragments' shape. Master moved three doc-only commits mid-merge, so a second merge brought those in. The diff against master is now exactly the lane's three files.
- `board.sh` did not conflict. Master has not touched it since the merge base.
- Re-ran both falsification layers against the fragment's new location. Layer 1: all 14 checks pass on this branch and all 14 fail against master's `board.sh`. Layer 2: every mutant trips its named check, with the cap mutant tripping the two cap checks as before.
- Full selftest on the pushed tree: 138 passed, 0 failed, my 14 included. Preflight passed with `--allow-tracker`.
- Patched the PR body's `Files:` line to name the fragment instead of `selftest.sh`, through the REST API since `gh pr edit` applies nothing here, and read it back.
- Pushed `cf854861fd`, removed `needs-rebase`, added `fold-ready`. The PR reads back non-draft with labels `harness` and `fold-ready`.

One mishap worth knowing: my first body patch used `#` as the sed delimiter, which the text contained, so an empty body briefly reached the PR. The second patch restored the full body and the read-back confirms it.
